cases.situation: My VP wants to move the whole team to a new project tool, Trackly, mid-quarter. I think it's a bad idea because our SOC 2 audit is Dec 9. Replying in the Slack thread.
cases.reply: I'm with you on the goal, Jira's been slowing us down. Where I land differently is the timing: with the SOC 2 audit on 9 December, I'd rather not move our evidence trail mid-quarter. Could we pilot Trackly with one squad now and move everyone in January? Happy to be told I'm overweighting the audit.
cases.note: One reason, the strongest, and a proposal that keeps the VP's goal intact.

cases.situation: 老公想把家里30万存款全部拿去买理财，我觉得应该留一部分做应急。想跟他说清楚又不想吵架。
cases.reply: 我明白你是想让钱多赚一点，这个我也想。我这边看法有点不一样：我觉得至少留8万做应急，万一谁工作有变动，不至于手忙脚乱。你是觉得放在理财里也能随时取出来吗？
cases.note: 先认同共同目标，只给一个理由，最后用真诚的问题听他的想法。

cases.situation: My dad keeps arguing with me about electric cars over text. He's getting worked up and I don't want to keep going back and forth.
cases.reply: I don't think we're going to agree on this one, Dad, and that's fine. I'd rather keep things easy between us than win the point. Still on for the game Sunday?
cases.note: When it escalates, stop adding reasons. Saying it once was enough.

cases.situation: 部门群里大家都赞成把周会从周三挪到周一早上8点半，领导也说挺好。我觉得不合适，因为我们组周一上午要跟华南区对账，想在群里说一下。
cases.reply: 周一开会，一周一开始就把重点对齐，这个思路我挺认同的。我这边有一个顾虑：我们组周一上午9点到11点要跟华南区对账，8点半开会很容易跟对账撞上。能不能改到周一下午2点？如果大家觉得早上更合适，我也想听听主要是考虑哪方面。
cases.note: 大家都赞成的方案，先认同目标，只讲自己组的一个具体冲突，给替代时间，再真心问对方的考虑。

cases.situation: Mon associé veut baisser tous nos prix de 20 % pour remplir le carnet de commandes d'ici décembre. On a une petite menuiserie, nos marges tournent autour de 25 %. Je pense que c'est une erreur mais je ne veux pas qu'on se braque.
cases.reply: Je suis d'accord avec toi qu'il faut remplir le carnet de commandes d'ici décembre. Là où je vois les choses autrement, c'est sur les 20 % : avec nos marges autour de 25 %, on travaillerait presque à perte sur chaque chantier. Qu'est-ce qui te fait penser que le prix est le frein principal ? Si tu as eu des retours de clients là-dessus, j'aimerais qu'on les regarde ensemble avant de trancher.
cases.note: Business partner: agree on the goal, give the one number that matters, then ask for his evidence instead of arguing.

cases.situation: My mother-in-law Linda keeps saying we should put our 4-month-old on his tummy to sleep because 'all my kids were fine'. Our pediatrician said back only. She's babysitting Saturday and I need to say something by text without starting a war.
cases.reply: Linda, thank you for taking Leo on Saturday, it's a real gift to have you. I know you raised three kids who slept on their tummies and turned out great. Where we land differently is that Dr. Shah was very clear that for Leo it's back only, and we'd feel much better sticking to that for every nap. Is there anything that makes back sleeping tricky for you with him? I'm happy to show you how we swaddle him so he settles.
cases.note: When the point isn't negotiable, aim the curiosity at practical obstacles, not at the rule itself.

cases.situation: GitHub code review. A senior engineer, Sam, commented on my PR asking me to switch our date formatting to moment.js. I think native Intl.DateTimeFormat is better: moment is in maintenance mode and would add a lot to our bundle. I don't want to look like I'm fighting a senior dev in a public thread.
cases.reply: Thanks, Sam, and agreed that we want one consistent way to format dates across the app. Where I land differently is the library: I'd lean towards native Intl.DateTimeFormat, mainly because moment is in maintenance mode and would add around 70 KB minified for the three formats we use. Is there a case you have in mind that Intl handles badly? If so, I'm happy to switch, or we can talk it through on a quick call.
cases.note: In a public review thread, the shared goal first, one reason with a number, then a real question that lets the senior person agree or correct you without losing face.

cases.situation: My 17-year-old daughter Ava just told me she's not applying to college this fall; she wants a gap year teaching at a surf school in Portugal. I actually like the gap year idea, I just think she should apply now and defer. She gets defensive fast.
cases.reply: I love that you want to do something real before more school, and honestly I think a gap year could be great for you. Where I land differently is the timing of applications: I'd rather you apply this fall and defer, because doing it now, with Ms Carter and your teachers around to help, is much easier than from Portugal next year. What worries you about applying now?
cases.note: With a teenager, agree with the part you genuinely support, disagree on one practical point, and end on a real question instead of a ruling.

cases.situation: I'm on our community garden committee. At last night's meeting everyone liked Frank's idea of spraying weed killer on the paths to save weeding time. The paths run right beside the plots the local school's kids grow food in. I want to post in our committee group chat.
cases.reply: I'm with Frank on the goal, weeding the paths eats most of our Saturday. Where I land differently is the spray: the paths run right alongside the school plots, and I'd rather not have weed killer anywhere near beds the kids eat from. Could we try cardboard and wood chips on the two worst paths this month and see if that does the job? If I've missed something about how it would be applied, tell me.
cases.note: Shared goal first, one strong reason, and a small trial instead of a vote against Frank, so he can agree without losing face in the group.
